submitter: bugs_open/257 round 2 — bugfix_257_token_budget_at_the_client lane (who-owns.py: OWNED by this lane, HANDOFF_2026-09-03 written by the previous session, research only, no code). This session implements that handoff's §5 steps 1 and 2 in one commit.
rationale:
THE DEFECT CLASS 257 FIXED CAME BACK IN A SHAPE THAT DEFEATS THE FIX, AND THE FLEET'S OWN INSTRUMENT CANNOT SEE IT.

Path A (2026-08-16, council APPROVED 366efae9, register MDL-041) moved output-token budget resolution into the provider clients: a caller that supplies NO budget now inherits ai_service.max_tokens from the config its client was constructed with. That is live and nothing here retracts it.

Two actions written AFTER it — rewrite_negations (2026-08-20, a5d5d0728) and repair_ordering_register (2026-08-31, f7156fb54) — each re-implemented the precedence rule by hand and each ended in `else { options["max_tokens"] = 2000 }`. Three things follow.

(a) THE LITERAL DEFEATS PATH A. An explicitly supplied option wins at the wire (platform/aiservice/anthropic.go:307). These callers ALWAYS supply one, so the client's new resolution never runs. A caller passing a literal is strictly WORSE OFF than one passing nil: nil now inherits the configuration, 2000 never can.

(b) THEY ARE THE FOURTH AND FIFTH COPIES OF ONE RULE, and llm_options.go's own SCOPE note predicted them in writing — 'a THIRD caller should be the extraction, not another paste'. Two more pastes arrived anyway. Neither reads the STEP's config; neither forwards budget_tokens. Both are strictly less capable than the helper sitting in the same Go package.

(c) THE LITERAL IS NUMERICALLY EQUAL TO THE CONFIGURED VALUE, so llm_call_log cannot tell a working config from a dropped one. offer-analyser declares ai_service.max_tokens=2000 on both steps that run repair_ordering_register; the Go fallback is also 2000. [MEASURED 2026-09-03] 29 calls, every one at max_tokens=2000, zero truncations, max output 600 tokens — a reading consistent with the code working AND equally consistent with the defect being live at that call site. No query over that table can separate them. The original 257 at least showed a WRONG number (2048 where config said 8000); this shows the RIGHT number for the wrong reason.

WHAT THE FIX IS. Delete both hand-rolled copies and call llmOptionsFromConfig, the resolver already in the same package. Then bind the rule at the PACKAGE so a sixth paste cannot merge quietly. Writing that package-wide test is what found two more sites the handoff's own census had misclassified and one it could not see at all:
  • companies_house_llm_review_action.go passed `map[string]interface{}{}` — an EMPTY options map. Not a burn (Path A covers it) but it drops the step's own max_tokens and budget_tokens, which no client constructor is ever shown.
  • execute_vision_prompt_action.go hand-read the key float64-only, with NO `> 0` guard, so a configured `max_tokens: 0` would be sent verbatim — a hard 400 from Anthropic.
  • feed_actions.go's Perplexity path hardcodes `"max_tokens": 4096` in a raw HTTP body. Invisible to every census this bug has run, because they all grepped for GenerateText and this path never touches platform/aiservice. It now reads source_config["max_tokens"], keeping 4096 as a DEFAULT — a fallback an operator can override rather than a number no config can reach.

BEHAVIOUR ON TODAY'S FLEET, measured rather than asserted. [MEASURED 2026-09-03, live agent_definitions, 208 active agents] every step reached by these five call sites: offer-analyser.repair_ordering_register 2000, offer-analyser.repair_hierarchy_register 2000, page-content-writer.rewrite_negations 16000, design-critique-agent.critique 16000, tool-acceptance-agent.look 4000, ch-llm-reviewer.review 2000 — ALL under ai_service, NONE at step top level, NONE declaring budget_tokens, and no active agent declares budget_tokens anywhere. So the helper's two extra capabilities (step-level precedence, budget_tokens forwarding) are inert today, and every one of these steps sends exactly the number it sends now. [MEASURED 2026-09-03, llm_call_log baseline pinned pre-change] repair_ordering_register 29 calls @2000; repair_hierarchy_register 6 @2000; rewrite_negations 3,245 @16000 and 99 @2000 (the 2000s are 2026-08-21..23, before migration 569 raised the CONFIG — 4 of them truncated, which is attributable to the configured value, not to the Go literal, and that distinction was only recoverable by reading migrations 517 and 569, never from the table); critique 5 @6000 + 1 @16000; look 91 @4000; ch_llm_review no rows.

THE SMALL BUDGET IS PRESERVED AS CONFIGURATION, NOT AS CODE. Migration 517's rationale for 2000 on rewrite_negations is sound (the answer is a few replacement sentences; a large ceiling only buys room for an essay the gate rejects) and migration 569 then raised it to 16000 on measured evidence from the 305 lane. That repair lives ONLY in configuration — which is the point: an operator moved it without a build. repair_ordering_register keeps its declared 2000. What is deleted is the pretence that the code decides.

ONE RESIDUAL BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, STATED: an UNCONFIGURED call at these sites would now reach aiservice.DefaultMaxOutputTokens (2048) via Path A instead of the literal 2000. [MEASURED] every live step declares the key, so this changes zero requests today; it is the correct direction regardless, because 2048 is the estate's single documented floor and 2000 was one action's opinion.

OUT OF SCOPE, DELIBERATELY. Candidate 2 (unifying ai_actions.go:357-360 with llmOptionsFromConfig) stays open: actions imports aiservice, so pushing the resolver down is an import cycle, and the two are not behaviourally equivalent (agent-level vs step-level precedence). This reduces the readers from five to two without touching that question. Also out of scope but FOUND and recorded: [MEASURED 2026-09-03] four site-adoption-agent steps declare a top-level config.max_tokens (32000/4000/6000/4000) and every one runs at the root ai_service 16000, because no reader looks there — analyze_site asks for double and gets it halved. That is the original 257 defect from the config end, it is a live config change with cost implications, and it is the owner's call, not a side effect of this commit. (The other three top-level declarations, html-developer-chunked's, ARE read — by getMaxTokens in html_actions.go — which answers a question the handoff left open.)

plan.summary: Delete every hand-rolled output-token budget in platform/orchestration/actions and route all five direct model callers through the package's ONE resolver (llmOptionsFromConfig), then bind that rule at the package with an AST audit that fails the build on a sixth paste. The literal being deleted is not a fallback: it wins over configuration at the wire, and in offer-analyser it is numerically equal to the configured value, so llm_call_log cannot distinguish a honoured config from a dropped one. Behaviour-neutral on every live step (each measured and enumerated in the rationale). Candidate 2 remains out of scope, with its import-cycle reason.

edits.rationale: Deletes the hand-rolled precedence block and its `else { options["max_tokens"] = 2000 }`. The literal is the load-bearing deletion: it wins at the wire, so this caller could never inherit configuration, and for three days in August it was numerically equal to the configured value. The step's declared 16000 (migration 569) is unaffected — [MEASURED] 3,245 calls already send 16000, so the config demonstrably reaches this action; what changes is that an UNCONFIGURED future caller of this action inherits 2048 instead of a private 2000. The comment that replaces the block says why, so the next author does not re-derive it.

Identical block, identical literal, added eleven days after the first. This is the call site where the literal and the configured value are the SAME number, so it is the one whose correctness could not be established by any query — 29 calls at 2000 is what both hypotheses predict. Removing the literal is what makes the instrument able to discriminate again: after this, changing offer-analyser's declared 2000 must move llm_call_log.max_tokens, and if it does not, the config is not arriving.

Passed a literal empty options map to GenerateText, once per batch. The handoff's census classified this site as 'reads config, no literal — acceptable'; it does not read config for the budget at all. Since Path A it is not a burn — the client resolves ai_service.max_tokens from its construction config, and ch-llm-reviewer declares 2000 — but an empty map still drops the STEP's max_tokens and budget_tokens, which no client constructor is ever shown, and it cannot emit the 'nobody sized this step' warning. One map per batch is retained deliberately: the client writes __sent_max_tokens/__usage_* back into the map it is handed, so a shared map would have each batch overwrite the previous batch's llm_call_log row.

edits.rationale: A fourth copy of the read, float64-only and — unlike every other copy — with NO `> 0` guard, so a configured `max_tokens: 0` would be sent verbatim and Anthropic returns a hard 400 (max_tokens.go states this). [MEASURED 2026-09-03] no active agent declares a non-positive budget, so this is a latent defect, not a live one; the helper closes it for free. The merge loop preserves the `model` key the surrounding code already put in the map.

Found BY the new audit, not by a human census: this path builds a raw HTTP body for Perplexity and never touches platform/aiservice, so every grep for GenerateText this bug has run was blind to it. It hardcoded `"max_tokens": 4096` in the request. Now reads source_config["max_tokens"], mirroring hours_lookback and max_items in the same struct, with 4096 kept as the default. sourceConfig is threaded in exactly as fetchViaResponsesAPI already receives it, so the signature change follows an existing precedent in the same file rather than inventing one. This is the honest distinction the whole submission turns on: a default an operator can override is not the same object as a literal no configuration can reach.

edits.rationale: The existing guard (TestNoProvocationActionCallsAModelWithAnEmptyOptionsMap) is well built — it refuses to pass when it matches nothing, the OPP-003 vacuity failure — but it is scoped to TWO NAMED FILES, so it could not see either new caller. This binds the rule at the PACKAGE. AST, not source text: a source scan would make this package's comments load-bearing, a documented failure shape here, so go/parser is asked for no comments at all. THE EXEMPTION IS NOT AN ALLOW-LIST OF VIOLATIONS: only ai_actions.go is exempt, because it IS the canonical resolver, and a third test asserts it still reads the key from config — the moment it stops, the exemption stops being granted. The two current violations are FIXED in this same commit, never allow-listed. MUTATION-PROVEN, four mutations in an isolated HEAD checkout: reinstating the literal fails; hand-rolling the map fails; passing nil fails; renaming the exempt file fails with the repoint message. The file states what it CANNOT see (a literal laundered through a variable; anything outside this package; config nobody reads).

The note said 'a THIRD caller should be the extraction, not another paste'. It was ignored twice. Corrected in place with a dated UPDATE rather than rewritten, per this estate's rule that a prediction which failed is evidence and must stay visible: it records that the extraction is now done for the direct callers, that what remains is ai_actions.go's inline block (candidate 2, blocked on an import cycle, not on willingness), and that a test now enforces what a comment could not.
